messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] High error rate + p95 latency spike for mariner-enterprise in eu-west-1 observed at 10:02 UTC. Affects dedicated VPC pool mariner-prod-eu. Pager routed to oncall. Runbook: regional failover checklist.
Alex (oncall): ack 10:03 — looking. I see 5xx rate up ~3x, p95 ~2.3s. Not seeing cluster OOMs. K8s nodes healthy.
Maya (sre): jumping in — any recent deploys? checking rollout history...
Sim (eng-runtime): no deploys in last 6h. Telemetry shows KV cache miss rate spiked for mariner tenant and some sustained queueing on the inference worker group eu-west-x02.
Alex (oncall): interesting — latency correlated with increased cold-starts of worker processes. Could be partial pod eviction + traffic still routed here.
Lina (product): Raj is on call with the Mariner SREs; they report increased tail latency from EU users and some session timeouts. They asked about failover options.
Raj (cs): confirmed — customer impact: web UI timeouts, 2-3% request failures, important live demo customers affected. They want a controlled failover to us-east as backup while we stabilize.
Maya (sre): propose staged traffic shift: weight-based routing -> 80/20 -> 50/50 -> 0/100 over 20 minutes, warm eu-west pods in drain mode, then cutover DNS TTL to 60s during shift. Thoughts?
Sim (eng-runtime): OK. We have a warm pool in us-east (reserved for mariner-dedicated) currently at 30% capacity. Need to scale to target capacity before shifting. I can trigger scale to 100% and pre-warm KV caches.
Alex (oncall): do we have automation to pre-warm? If not, will need to route synthetic traffic to populate KV and model caches.
Sim (eng-runtime): we do have prewarm job: `jobs/prewarm-mariner.sh --region=us-east --parallel=8`. Will run now. Logs: starting 10:09.
Maya (sre): I'll update routing policy in TrafficManager to staged weights. Current policy: `tm-policy mariner-prod-eu: 100% eu-west`. I'll prepare patch to add weighted endpoints.
Lina (product): we should coordinate messaging. I'll draft a short notification: "Planned staged traffic shift to backup region to mitigate latency impact. No expected data loss." CC Raj for customer wording.
Raj (cs): thanks, Lina. I'll send interim note: "We're initiating a staged failover to a backup region to improve performance; we'll keep you updated every 10 min." Sending now.
Alex (oncall): prewarm job reports 95% cache hit after ~4m. us-east workers healthy. Sim, please confirm model KV warmed and embedding index loaded.
Sim (eng-runtime): confirmed: KV cache 98% hit, embedding index warmed, latency in us-east test bench ~120ms p95. Ready for gradual traffic shift.
Maya (sre): executing routing patch now — applying `tm update mariner-prod --weights eu-west=80 us-east=20 --ttl=60` 10:16. Pushing to canary control-plane.
Incident Bot: DeployBot: traffic-manager update started (deploy_id: tm-6421). Rolling change — monitors attached.
Alex (oncall): watch logs/metrics for error spike. If 5xx > 5% or p95 > 2s for 2 consecutive mins, rollback.
Maya (sre): 10:18 metrics: error down to 1.2%, p95 down to 1.4s. Good sign. Proceed to next step in 5m.
Lina (product): customer update sent 10:20: "Traffic shifting in stages to backup region; improvements expected within minutes." Raj said they appreciated the quick heads-up.
Raj (cs): customer asked about DNS TTL implications — they said some clients have long caching but most saw improvement already. Keep an eye on API gateway logs for stale sessions.
Sim (eng-runtime): starting next weight change at 10:23 -> eu-west=50 us-east=50. Executing `tm update mariner-prod --weights eu-west=50 us-east=50`.
Maya (sre): 10:24 monitors: p95 eu-west=1.1s, us-east=130ms; global p95 ~650ms, errors 0.8%. No anomalies.
Alex (oncall): good. Plan: after 10 minutes of stability, move to full 0/100 and then perform DNS cutover to set primary to us-east (TTL 60) and then increase to 300 once stable.
Katelyn (next-oncall): noting for handoff — If anything regresses during final cut, I'll be next to handle escalation.
Sim (eng-runtime): initiating final shift at 10:33 -> eu-west=0 us-east=100. `tm update mariner-prod --weights eu-west=0 us-east=100` in flight.
Incident Bot: DeployBot: traffic-manager update complete (tm-6421) 10:34.
Maya (sre): confirm global p95 140ms, errors 0.2%. Running DNS update to point primary A records at us-east LB now. Using split-horizon to avoid internal loopbacks.
Alex (oncall): DNS change: `nsupdate` script applied, TTL remains 60 for 10 min. Log: `nsupdate -k /secrets/dns.key ...` 10:35.
Raj (cs): customer advised 10:36: "We see improved performance; thanks. We'll monitor on our side." They asked for a short post-incident note after stabilization.
Lina (product): we'll prepare a postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps; include recommendation to increase warm pool minimum for mariner to 70% during EU peak hours.
Sim (eng-runtime): note: discovered prewarm job occasionally times out under burst — raising an action item to make prewarm idempotent and more parallel.
Alex (oncall): handing off to Katelyn for monitoring window and post-incident follow-up. Handoff notes: region failback completed, TTL 60, caches warmed, customer notified. Conditions for re-open: errors >1% sustained 3m or p95 >1.5s.
Katelyn (next-oncall): ack handoff 10:40. I'll monitor for 2 hours and draft the incident summary with timeline. Adding action items to backlog: prewarm hardening, automated capacity gating, customer communication template.
Incident Bot: Incident resolved: Severity reduced to S2 (customer impact mitigated). Auto-close check in 2h if stable.
Alex (oncall): thanks team. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
